chunks: A man said to Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar, peace be upon them: “Promise me.”
He said: “How can I promise you, when I have more hope in what I do not expect than in what I do expect?”

key_terms.أَرْجَى: More likely to be hoped for; more expected in comparison.
key_terms.أَعِدُكَ: I promise you; I give you my word.
key_terms.عِدْنِي: Promise me; give me your assurance.
key_terms.كَيْفَ: How; expressing the difficulty or impossibility of doing so.

ai.seo_question: What does Imam Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام teach about hope and human expectation?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a teaching about the uncertainty of worldly expectation and the limits of human assurance. It reflects a perspective of humility before divine decree, where what one does not anticipate may be more likely than what one confidently expects.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3610 - A man said to Abu al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as):
"Promise me something."
Imam (as) replied: "How can I promise you, when I have more hope in what I do not expect than in what I do expect?"
